title: Decide with the flags in view: Advance acknowledges them, the record keeps them
deviations_from_card: 8 cases = the card's 7 + the critic's editor case (a 409 rolls the optimistic pick back via settleDisposition; the pick, the note autosave, the blur and the keepalive flush all build their body with dispositionPatchBody, so each carries `acknowledged`. A source guard forbids the old hand-built `{ disposition, note }` body). Case 6 (note-only edit of a stored advance is never gated) was already green at base, so it is a guard: 7 of 8 red before. The door enforces only the advance-ack half, as the card's flow step 4 says. The strong-read pass reason is an editor gate (case 3 is pure). Only an advance or pass that CHANGES the disposition writes decision_basis. A note-only edit keeps the basis it annotates, and hold/clear NULL it. The route test lives in the existing analyses-routes.test.ts, as the critic allowed. perf-budget.json: page.tsx maxModules 1424 -> 1425 (the one new module), KB ceiling unchanged. The tests were meant to land in their own test(...) commit, but commit-msg rejected that subject, so they landed in the feat commit b0a3b711c.
notes: core.ts committed alone under the lock (7486cd769, one ALTER at the end of the second migration list). api-response.ts (DISPOSITION_ACK_REQUIRED appended at the end of REFUSAL_ERRORS) and the 4 catalogs (report.decision* x4 + errors.DISPOSITION_ACK_REQUIRED, real cs/de/fr) committed together under the lock (b3ea628d6). The doc went in under the lock (a02b860d3). Perf was measured with git archive: HEAD 1424 modules/9023 KB vs HEAD + this card alone 1425/9032. The task-hub routes grew +1 KB each (the pipeline.ts hunk). The analyses/[slug] route grew +43 KB (decisionBrief -> sanity-checks/format), far under its 3103 ceiling. The committed tree after b0a3b711c measures findings []. The working-tree test:perf overages (~13 KB on 12 task-hub routes) come from siblings' UNCOMMITTED billing/devcase files, not from this card. In full test:unit, recipes-literals fails on the sibling's uncommitted SetupFinishReceipt.tsx (shell-setup-wizard), and the spawn tree-kill test is a FLAKE. Neither touches these files. tsc whole-tree errors are only in sibling in-flight tests (devcase-stage-outcome, setupFinishOutcome, kpi-sim). Known limit: the PATCH is read-then-write without .immediate(). The gate's input (the payload's warns) is immutable, and the stored-disposition check only decides whether a gate applies, so a race can at worst skip one ack prompt for a concurrent same-disposition write. The editor's checkboxes start unticked even when an advance is already stored. That is harmless, because re-saving a stored advance is never gated.
